problem:
$$
{U}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 10\end{aligned}],\,{V}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A={U}_{r}{Σ}_{r}{V}_{r}^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$

activity_context.topic_title: Singular Value Decomposition and the Pseudoinverse Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Pseudoinverse of a Matrix Given Its Reduced Singular Value Decomposition
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14095495/assets/95ef5c6139d13a561125764fc1658d03748004b4ee28843a7a3eb8dc7a37504a.png)
Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=U_r \Sigma_r V_r^T$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse $A^+.$
examples.worked_solution:
If $A=U_r \Sigma_r V_r ^T$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V_r \, \Sigma_r^+ \, U_r^T,
$$

where $\Sigma_r^+$ is the pseudoinverse of $\Sigma_r.$

First, notice that

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14095495/assets/b9efcf7d8dfaa697ebbed69113611e3e669b8c7da27813a9262a7e4e5542dbeb.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}12 & 16 & 0 \\ 9 & 12 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{10} & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & =V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
